By Austin Parsons

Overview

Sedans are falling out of favor, but the Nissan Altima is sticking around for 2026 nonetheless, bringing the well-rounded and value-focused disposition that it has been offering the segment for decades. While the Altima won't take home any awards for being particularly quick or engaging to drive, it hits all the key targets for mass consumption: it's affordable, practical, comfortable, and attractively styled.

Other mid-size sedans, such as the Honda Accord and Toyota Camry, are far better driver's cars, even if that isn't their primary aim. The Altima's standard four-cylinder and continuously variable transmission are unimpressive, but for one saving grace: fuel efficiency. While many rivals have adopted hybrid technology to eke out additional MPGs, the Altima is still impressively efficient without any electrification. For most family-sedan shoppers, the Altima scratches most of the right itches, but the Honda and Toyota do that and go beyond.

Expert Tip: Another sedan to consider is the Hyundai Sonata, which features a much nicer 191-hp four-cylinder engine mated to a smooth-shifting, conventional automatic transmission. It starts at just a few hundred dollars more than the Altima.

What's New for 2026?

For 2026, Nissan has pared down the Altima lineup to just two trim levels: SV and SR. In addition to removing the top and bottom trims, a Midnight Edition package is newly available for the SR trim. It is primarily cosmetic, adding a two-tone black roof, darkened window trim, black wheels, darkened badges, and black 19-inch wheels. A dual-zone automatic climate control system and a sunroof also come as part of the Midnight Edition package.

C/D Expert Tip:

If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.

Pricing and Which One to Buy

As the Altima is already one of the most affordable options in the mid-size sedan segment, we'd shell out the additional $1500 for the more premium SR trim. For the upcharge, you get sportier exterior styling with black trim accents, a sportier suspension, 19-inch wheels, a larger 12.3-inch touchscreen infotainment display with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto integration, a wireless charging pad, and two rear USB ports. We'd skip over the new SR Midnight Edition; if you'd like all-wheel drive, it's a $1500 option.

Engine, Transmission, and Performance

  • Engine: 188-hp 2.5-liter four-cylinder
  • Transmission: continuously variable automatic transmission (CVT)
  • Drivetrains: front-wheel drive, all-wheel drive

All 2026 Altimas come with a 2.5-liter four-cylinder engine making 188 horsepower. The power is funneled through a continuously variable automatic transmission (CVT). The CVT robs the fun of using the paddle shifters on equipped trims, and the four-cylinder can make some unruly engine noises when pressed to the limit. But this isn’t the kind of car one should be pushing that hard, anyway. When we last tested an Altima back in 2023, we were unimpressed with its unrefined engine and numb steering, but noted that its ride was remarkably comfortable, even on large 19-inch wheels.

0–60-MPH Times

  • C/D 60-mph Test: 7.6 seconds (SL AWD)

In Comparison: An all-wheel-drive Altima that we tested in 2023 needed 7.6 seconds to hit 60 mph at our test track. That is almost a second slower than the last Honda Accord Touring Hybrid that we tested, which hit the 60 mph mark in 6.7 seconds.

Fuel Economy and Real-World MPG

  • C/D 75-mph Highway Fuel-Economy Test: 35 mpg (SL AWD)
  • EPA City Ratings: 25-27 mpg
  • EPA Highway Ratings: 34-37 mpg

The Altima has long made lofty fuel economy part of its appeal to car shoppers, without resorting to a hybrid or plug-in-hybrid powertrain. While the EPA hasn’t yet issued estimates for the 2026 Altima yet, last year's model in standard front-wheel drive configuration returned an EPA-estimated 27 mpg city and 37 highway in the SL and SV trims. With all-wheel drive, those EPA estimates dropped to 25 mpg city and 34 mpg on the highway. On our 75-mph highway fuel-economy route—part of our extensive testing regimen—an all-wheel-drive Altima achieved an impressive 35 mpg. For more information about the Altima's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.

Interior, Comfort, and Cargo

First Row: The Altima's cabin is comfortable and agreeable. User-friendly switchgear dots the straightforward dashboard, and the overall quality of the interior materials is good rather than flashy. There’s decent storage up front, with narrow, albeit deep, door pockets and a useful tray on the center console.

Second Row: Large rear seats provide plenty of legroom. Unfortunately, the Nissan's rear seats don't fold completely flat, and they must be released using handles in the trunk, which is inconvenient.

Cargo Capacity: We fit six carry-on bags in the Altima's trunk and 17 bags total with the rear seats folded. These numbers matched those of the Toyota Camry we tested, but both the Altima and Camry fell short of the Accord's 19 bags.

View Interior Photos

Infotainment and Connectivity

  • Infotainment: 8.0-inch touchscreen (SV), 12.3-inch touchscreen (SR)
  • Connectivity: Bluetooth, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto
  • Audio System: 6-speaker audio system (standard), 9-speaker Bose audio system (optional)

The Altima’s standard 8.0-inch touchscreen has Apple CarPlay and Android Auto capability. The infotainment interface has a customizable main menu but otherwise few personalization options. While the sound system has useful knobs for volume and tuning, the touchscreen we tested responded slowly to inputs. The SV trim now comes with a 12.3-inch touchscreen, a wireless phone charger, and two rear USB ports as standard equipment. A six-speaker system is the Altima's base audio setup, but a nine-speaker Bose audio system is available on the SR trim and comes included in the SR Premium Package.

Safety and Driver-Assistance Features

Overall Safety Rating (NHTSA)

View Crash Test Results

Every Altima has forward-collision warning and automated emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring, high-beam assist, rear cross-traffic alert, and more. Nissan also offers a semi-autonomous drive mode called ProPilot Assist.

  • Standard Safety Features: lane-departure warning with available lane-keeping assist, rear automated emergency braking
  • Optional Safety Features: adaptive cruise control

For information about the Altima's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.

Warranty and Maintenance Coverage

The Altima has competitive warranty coverage that aligns with rivals such as the Honda Accord and Toyota Camry. Nissan has also stepped up with a new complimentary maintenance program that provides up to three scheduled oil changes for two years or 24,000 miles, whichever comes first.

  • Limited Warranty: three years or 36,000 miles
  • Powertrain Warranty: five years or 60,000 miles
  • Complimentary Maintenance: two years or 24,000 miles of complimentary oil changes
